# evolve

[arc reference](../index.md) › [Products](../index.md#products) › **Product**

## Why it exists

```tagline
The test kitchen. It tries a new recipe next to the old one, counts what the customers actually did,
and only then suggests a change. It never rewrites the menu itself.
```

# Start here

## In plain words

Think of arc as a small company whose staff are AI models. Sooner or later someone says: "I think this
part could be better."

Everyone has a hunch. A hunch is not proof. So arc has a test kitchen for hunches.

```panel big
**evolve is the test kitchen.** It runs a fair taste test, and it has three strict habits:

- **Two recipes, side by side.** The old one (the champion) and the new one (the challenger). Never one, never three.
- **One count, decided in advance.** The way the result is judged is fixed before the test starts, and it is worked out once. A "no" is written down too, so nobody can keep re-counting until the answer flips.
- **It never touches the menu.** When the new recipe wins, evolve only leaves a note in your inbox. A person decides. This holds even for taking a bad change back out.
```

### An example (an illustration, not a real run)

Say arc wants to test a new wording for one of its own prompts. evolve opens a test: old wording on one
half of the real jobs, new wording on the other half. Results are logged as they come in. When there
is enough evidence, evolve counts once. If the new wording is clearly better, you get a note that says
"here is a proposed change". If it is not clearly better, the "no" is recorded and the old wording stays.

### Why this needs to be a product at all

Without a rule, "did this help?" is one person squinting at a chart. evolve replaces that squint with
one fixed test, and it takes every check to pass together: enough samples on both sides, a clear win,
no safety limit crossed, and no half-finished measurement. Passing just because nothing looked wrong is
not enough.

Its results are also read back from arc's logbook, which nobody can quietly edit. So the count can be
re-checked later by anyone.

Honest status: the engine is built and tested on sample data, but no real venture has fed it real
results yet. The room in the face app carries the badge "fixture-proven, unexercised", and that is
deliberate.

## arc words → normal words

```lede
Eleven pieces of arc jargon. Each is an ordinary test-kitchen thing wearing a technical name.
```

```rosetta
module | a product that has signed up for testing | it must declare which files may be tested
surface | the one dish being tested | points at exactly one target file
experiment | one taste test | exactly two recipes compared on one surface
arm | one recipe in the test | a tag like `+champion` or `+challenger-a`
champion / challenger | the old recipe / the new one | the result is always new minus old
cohort | which half of the tasters a unit is in | one half explores, the other half decides the result
seal | a photo of the dish before the test | if the file changes mid-test, the numbers mean nothing
verdict | the one-time answer | recorded once, even when it is a "no"
propose-only | the kitchen writes a note, never the menu | evolve has no code path that edits a real file
spine / receipt | arc's logbook / one line in it | every measurement is a receipt, read back to judge the test
MISSING | nothing was measured here | shown as MISSING, never quietly counted as zero
```

```gloss
hash: a fingerprint of some text; change one letter and the fingerprint changes.
digest: a short fingerprint of exactly what a command is about to write.
```

## How a job flows

```lede
A test has three moves: open it, feed it results, count once. Turning a win into a real change is a
separate road, and a human walks it.
```

```flow
source: arc-evolve open
box: ① Open | seal the target, name two arms
box: ② Measure | log results as they arrive
box*: ③ Count once | the fixed test decides
box: ④ Propose | a note in your inbox
labels: sealed, enough data, winner
out: file changed | test is void
out: not enough data | no verdict yet
out: a "no" | recorded, old recipe stays
out+: promotion.proposed | a human merges or declines
divider: 3 | machine only measures | a human decides
note: The machine never writes the change. That step always belongs to a person.
caption: Figure 1 — one experiment, start to proposal. | The dashed line is where measuring ends and a human decision begins.
```

## The stages, one by one

```lede
Each stage is written twice: first what it does in ordinary words, then what actually happens.
```

```steps
t: Open the test
plain: Pick one dish and two recipes. evolve takes a photo of the dish as it is now, so it can tell later if anyone changed it mid-test. There is a cap on how many tests one product can run at once, and every test has a time limit.
d: The module names the surface, the target file and the two arms. The seal is a hash of the target file's bytes. Each unit of work is put in an arm by a fingerprint of the experiment and unit ids, never by a coin flip, so the same unit always lands in the same arm.
f: `.claude/scripts/evolve/arc-evolve.mjs` · `.claude/scripts/evolve/assign.mjs` · ADR-0303 · ADR-0310

t: Feed it results
plain: Each result says: this unit, this measure, this dated window. A result with nothing actually observed is refused. Where nothing was measured, the board says MISSING rather than a fake zero.
d: Each call reports one value for one metric over one window, and arc-evolve computes the arm and cohort itself. The board folds every receipt on the spine into the true status of each experiment.
f: `.claude/scripts/evolve/wire.mjs` · `.claude/scripts/evolve/board.mjs` · ADR-0304

t: Count once
plain: One fixed statistical test compares the two recipes. The new recipe must win clearly, not narrowly, and every side condition must hold. The answer is written down whether it is yes or no.
d: The gate in `verdict.mjs` needs the lower bound to clear the declared floor, the point difference to reach the minimum effect, enough units in both arms, no guardrail breached and no missing windows. The test is `newcombe-wilson-difference-v1`, pinned by ADR-0306 and ADR-0311.
f: `.claude/scripts/evolve/verdict.mjs` · ADR-0306 · ADR-0311

t: Propose, then a human decides
plain: A winner becomes a note in your inbox. If you merge it, the merged file must be exactly what was proposed, or it is refused. After that, evolve keeps watching that what is served still matches.
d: A proposal needs a live ticket: the seal still matches, and the file is on the module's allowed list. If the file later drifts to something unexplained, or the win degrades, the result is again a proposal or a "manual intervention" incident. It is never a machine patch.
f: `.claude/scripts/evolve/lineage.mjs` · ADR-0305
```

# The bigger loop

## Plan first, then write

```lede
Every command that writes has a dry run. You read what it would do, then confirm with its fingerprint.
```

`open`, `measure` and `conclude` each run in two passes. Without `--expect`, the command only prints a
plan and a digest. Run it again with `--expect` and that digest, and it re-reads the logbook as it is
now. It writes only if the plan is still exactly the same. If the world moved in between, it stops and
writes nothing (ADR-1340).

`arc-evolve` is a command-line tool, not a slash command. evolve declares no `/arc-*` commands and no
agents of its own.

## Built before it had anything to run

The rule in arc says a self-improvement engine should sleep until a real venture has weeks of real
results. At kickoff that was not yet true. The owner saw the evidence and chose to build anyway. So
evolve was built on sample data, and the missing real feed was recorded as missing. A made-up feed was
rejected on purpose, because invented data would spoil the very count evolve exists to protect.

The same reasoning is behind the propose-only rule. After a promotion a person may have hand-edited
the file. A machine holding an old patch would silently wipe that edit out (ADR-0305).

## What it grows into

The same idea is used to check arc's own council: `calibrate.mjs` compares the confidence the council
states with how often it turned out right, and says "insufficient evidence" when there is too little to
judge (ADR-0307).
